Subject: Aurora Systems — initial access governance & staging ownership (SSO/SCIM sweep)

Hi Alex —

Thanks for the quick conversation on the call earlier. I wanted to capture the immediate next steps so we can align sequencing and owners for the staging cutover. Primary goals for the first sprint: get SSO (SAML) validated in staging, enable SCIM provisioning for the initial user group, and confirm IP allowlist ranges for token endpoints.

Proposed sequencing (high level):
- Week 0: Exchange SAML metadata and test IdP-to-SP sign-on in staging (okta → Redwood).
- Week 1: SCIM service account provisioning + permissioning for group sync (least privilege).
- Week 2: IP allowlist confirmation + canary rollout (10% of sessions).

Attachments: I’ve uploaded a one-page mutual action plan (MAP_Aurora_v1.xlsx) to the Drive link below; it includes owner fields and tentative dates.

Ask: Can you confirm the SAML metadata file (entity ID / ACS URL) and an Okta admin contact who can perform the export? Also, do you have CIDR ranges we should add to our allowlist for staging?

I’ll loop in Monica and Jonas to draft a lightweight runbook and can share a snippet for your review by end of day tomorrow.

Thanks —
Priyom Das
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
pri_yom@redwood.com

Attachments: MAP_Aurora_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Subject: Re: Aurora Systems — initial access governance & staging ownership (SSO/SCIM sweep)

Thanks Alex — cc’ing internal delivery owners so we can map tasks to the runbook. A couple of notes from Redwood side:

- Order of ops: we recommend SSO validation in staging before enabling SCIM for bulk sync. SCIM requires a scoped service account with token rotation; we’ll provide an example IAM policy.
- Service accounts: plan for one SCIM service account scoped only to user/group write operations, no broader org admin privileges.
- IP allowlist: once CIDRs are confirmed we’ll add them to staging egress rules and schedule a short smoke test window.
- Rollback triggers: auth error rate > 5% or significant auth latency (token handshake > 500ms) should trigger immediate rollback.

I’m attaching a short runbook snippet (runbook_snippet.md) with the concrete steps we’ll hand to Aurora’s Okta admin. I’ll publish a full staging playbook to the Drive link and update the MAP with owner names.

Monica Patel
Implementation Lead — Customer Success | Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com

Attachment: runbook_snippet.md (markdown stub)

Alex — great, thanks for confirming. Summary & next steps below (publishing to the Drive MAP now):

1) Docs/SOW: you mentioned DocuSign — thanks; we’ll assume SOW countersigned by 2027-06-15. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/98721 (I’ll add the MAP link).
2) Dates: Dry-run Thu Jun 17 (SRE + Redwood), Staging canary Sun Jun 20 (start 1300 PDT).
3) Auth config: we’ll validate SAML metadata in staging on Jun 10–11, then request SCIM service account creation (90-day rotation window as requested).
4) Allowlist: Redwood will add 54.210.12.0/22 and 3.120.45.0/24 for staging endpoints.

Can you confirm the dry-run duration you’d like (30 vs 60 mins) and a point-of-contact for the canary window (name + mobile)? I’ll share a one-page readiness checklist and the runbook snippet before Thu.

Thanks — looking forward to the dry-run.
